title.en: Recall pigments, stored food and examples

say.en: Some seaweeds grow as tall as trees and are brown; others live deep in the sea and are red. Their colour tells us which pigments they carry. In this lesson: Compare Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae.
Recall pigments, stored food and examples.

body.en: *Green algae* have chlorophyll a and b in chloroplasts of various shapes. Most have pyrenoids, which store protein and starch. Their cell wall has an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose. Examples: Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra and Chara.
body.kn: ಹಸಿರು ಶೈವಲಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಹರಿತ್ತು a ಮತ್ತು b. ಪೈರಿನಾಯ್ಡ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಪಿಷ್ಟ ಸಂಗ್ರಹ. ಉದಾ: ಕ್ಲಾಮಿಡೊಮೊನಾಸ್, ವಾಲ್ವಾಕ್ಸ್, ಸ್ಪೈರೋಗೈರಾ, ಕಾರಾ.

narration.en: Sea water absorbs red light within the first few metres, while blue and green light go much deeper. Green algae (chlorophyll a and b) need red and blue light and live near the surface; brown algae use fucoxanthin to catch blue-green light; red algae use r-phycoerythrin to catch green-blue light and can live at great depths.
narration.kn: ಸಮುದ್ರದ ನೀರು ಮೊದಲ ಕೆಲವು ಮೀಟರ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲೇ ಕೆಂಪು ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ಹೀರುತ್ತದೆ, ನೀಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಹಸಿರು ಬೆಳಕು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಆಳಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಹಸಿರು ಶೈವಲಗಳು (ಕ್ಲೋರೋಫಿಲ್ a, b) ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಬಳಿ; ಕಂದು ಶೈವಲಗಳು ಫ್ಯೂಕೋಕ್ಸಾಂಥಿನ್‌ನಿಂದ ನೀಲಿ-ಹಸಿರು ಬೆಳಕು ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತವೆ; ಕೆಂಪು ಶೈವಲಗಳು r-ಫೈಕೋಎರಿತ್ರಿನ್‌ನಿಂದ ಹಸಿರು-ನೀಲಿ ಬೆಳಕು ಹಿಡಿದು ಬಹಳ ಆಳದಲ್ಲೂ ಬದುಕುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: On the board: Classes of algae

say.en: We compare the three classes of algae in a table.
Green algae have chlorophyll a and b, and store starch in pyrenoids.
Brown algae have chlorophyll a and c with fucoxanthin, and store laminarin or mannitol.
Red algae have chlorophyll a and d with r-phycoerythrin, and store floridean starch.
A brown alga like a kelp has a holdfast, a stipe and a frond.

explanation.en: The three classes differ in pigments, stored food, cell wall and flagella. Brown algae such as kelps can be very large; red algae are mostly marine and can live at great depths.

say.en: Sort the algae by their colour class.

body.en: *Brown algae* are mostly marine and range from simple filaments like Ectocarpus to huge kelps. They have chlorophyll a and c, carotenoids and the brown pigment fucoxanthin. Food is stored as laminarin or mannitol. The body has a holdfast, a stalk called the stipe, and a leaf-like frond. Examples: Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum, Fucus.
body.kn: ಕಂದು ಶೈವಲಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಹರಿತ್ತು a, c ಮತ್ತು ಫ್ಯೂಕೋಜ಼ಾಂಥಿನ್. ಆಹಾರ ಲ್ಯಾಮಿನಾರಿನ್ ಅಥವಾ ಮ್ಯಾನಿಟಾಲ್. ದೇಹದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೋಲ್ಡ್‌ಫಾಸ್ಟ್, ಸ್ಟೈಪ್, ಫ್ರಾಂಡ್.

problem.en: A marine alga has a holdfast, a stipe and a frond, contains fucoxanthin, and stores mannitol. Identify its class and give one example.

steps.en: Fucoxanthin is the brown pigment of Phaeophyceae.
Mannitol or laminarin as stored food also fits brown algae.
Holdfast, stipe and frond are the typical parts of a large brown alga such as Laminaria.
